newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end lower, SBI in limelight.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end lower, SBI in limelight.

text.p: ** (1300 GMT) Indian shares close lower, focus on select
blue-chips
** Bombay index falls 0.96 pct, National bourse 1.21 pct,
Calcutta 0.43 pct, Madras 0.85 pct and Delhi 0.53 pct
** Bank stock SBI in market limelight, dealers keenly await
pricing of its GDR issue in U.S. later today
** Market likely to remain stuck in narrow price band, dull
volumes, traders say
Shares across Indian bourses finished lower on Thursday with market action limited to select blue-chip stocks, traders said.
"There is no major factor playing in the market -- some expectations about fresh buying didn't materialise," said dealer Dheeraj Agarwal at SSKI Securities in Bombay.
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) 30-share index fell 31.03 points or 0.96 percent to 3,195.77, a touch above its intra-day low of 3,190.36.
Dealers said bank stock SBI which will price its $400 million GDR issue in the U.S later today was in market focus.
Selling by some foreign funds dragged the SBI stock 10.75 rupees lower to 239.0, after hitting the day's high of 252.75 in volumes of 8.5 million shares.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index lost 11.35 points or 1.21 percent to 936.27. The CRISIL 500-share index finished 6.06 points lower at 617.38.

Telecom stock MTNL and tobacco major ITC bucked the losing trend to close higher. Fund buying in MTNL pushed it up 7.50 rupees to 213.0 and heavy speculative buying by Calcutta-based operators helped ITC gain 10.50 to 312.75, traders said.
The Calcutta index fell 1.84 points to 421.54.
At the Delhi Stock Exchange, share prices closed lower on lack of strong buying support as institutional investors stayed on the sideline in a day of thin trade, dealers said.
The Delhi index was 3.75 points lower at 715.99.
The Madras index dropped 28.51 points or 0.85 percent to 3,344.76.
Dealers said lack of major market-moving news will keep the market in a narrow range, with focus on select blue-chips.
"The outlook for the market continues to remain dull and weak," SSKI's Agarwal said.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
